_why: CK-ui-state asks its five questions of THREE named components per page (C1/C2/C3), but every component-state prover measured the PAGE and would have banked one reading against all three subjects — the 'one measurement swept two views' error that put V1's verdicts on 14 V2 rows earlier in this arc. A subject cannot be measured until it can be SELECTED, and the bank's own subject.seen refs only carry a real CSS selector for 39 of 66; the other 27 are prose ('hive_members read', 'grid render'). This file is the missing structure: the live-resolved selector for each component, discovered by loading all 22 pages signed-in and reading the DOM, then verified to resolve before being trusted.
_rules: on_load=true means the component is rendered by the page's own load path, so the loading/skeleton/busy/populated oracles have a real subject.

on_load=false means it only exists after a person opens something (a modal, a tab, a form). Its load-state oracles have NO subject and bank declared-na with that reason — never green, which would be vacuity, and never failed, which would be a fabricated defect.

Every selector here must RESOLVE live or it does not belong in this file; unresolved components stay owed with the reason recorded, because a selector that matches nothing measures nothing while looking like coverage.
